claims.text: The presence of explanations in LLM responses increases user reliance on correct LLM answers.
The presence of explanations in LLM responses increases user overreliance on incorrect LLM answers.
Providing clickable sources in LLM responses increases appropriate user reliance on correct LLM answers.
Providing clickable sources in LLM responses decreases user overreliance on incorrect LLM answers.
Inconsistencies within LLM explanations reduce user overreliance on incorrect LLM answers compared to consistent explanations.
The presence of explanations or sources in LLM responses increases user self-reported confidence in their final answers.
The presence of explanations or sources in LLM responses decreases the likelihood of users writing follow-up questions.
Actively clicking on provided source links increases task accuracy when the LLM answer is incorrect.

evidence.description: In the absence of sources, when the LLM answer was correct, participants' task accuracy was higher when an explanation was provided (78.2%) compared to when no explanation was provided (67.2%).
In the absence of sources, when the LLM answer was incorrect, participant accuracy was lower when an explanation was provided (17.2%) compared to when no explanation was provided (21.8%).
In the absence of an explanation, when the LLM answer was correct, agreement was higher when sources were provided (73.4%) than when not provided (67.2%).
In the absence of an explanation, when the LLM answer was incorrect, agreement was lower when sources were provided (68.2%) than when not provided (78.2%).

When participants received an inconsistent explanation for an incorrect LLM answer, agreement with the LLM was significantly lower (69.7% vs 83.3%, p=.002) and accuracy was significantly higher (30.3% vs 16.7%, p=.002) compared to receiving a consistent explanation.
Providing an explanation led to significantly higher confidence ratings (5.26 vs 4.55 on a 1-7 scale, p<.001), and providing sources similarly increased confidence ratings (5.50 vs 4.55, p<.001).
Participants were significantly less likely to write a follow-up question when explanations were present (28.2% vs 71.4%, p<.001) or when sources were present (34.4% vs 71.4%, p<.001).
When provided with sources and an incorrect LLM answer, participants who clicked on sources achieved 37.0% accuracy compared to 24.2% accuracy for those who did not click.

methodologies.name: Think-Aloud Exploratory Study (Study 1)
methodologies.description: A preliminary qualitative think-aloud study observed 16 participants using ChatGPT (GPT-4o) across multi-turn interactions to answer objective questions and identify key response features shaping reliance.
conditions: Part 1: Base question answering with free-form interactions
Part 2: Question answering with suggested follow-up prompting strategies

methodologies.name: Controlled 2x2x2 Within-Subjects Experiment (Study 2)
methodologies.description: A pre-registered, controlled within-subjects experiment with 308 participants evaluating the effects of LLM answer accuracy, explanation presence, and source link presence on reliance, accuracy, and user perception.
datasets: 12 binary factual questions derived from National Geographic Kids Weird But True books
conditions: LLM Answer Accuracy: Correct vs Incorrect
Clickable Sources Presence: Present vs Absent

limitations.text: The studies were conducted solely in the context of objective question-answering and may not generalize to other LLM usage contexts such as writing, idea generation, or task automation.
The think-aloud setup in Study 1 may have caused participants to behave reactively, resulting in a substantially higher source-clicking rate (63.8%) than observed in the online experiment (25.8%).
Study 2 presented single controlled LLM responses rather than allowing dynamic multi-turn interactions, which does not fully reflect real-world interactive LLM usage over time.
The LLM's accuracy in Study 2 was fixed at 50% for experimental balance, which is significantly lower than current state-of-the-art model performance.
Task questions were intentionally selected to be difficult (human pilot accuracy <50%), so findings may not generalize to tasks where users possess sufficient domain knowledge.

future_work.text: Investigate how user reliance is shaped across other generative AI tasks beyond objective question-answering, such as creative writing, brainstorming, and task automation.
Develop and evaluate computational interventions that automatically detect and highlight inconsistencies and other unreliability cues in LLM explanations.
Explore different source design choices (such as source placement, preview amount, and handling of fake or conflicting sources) and their impact on user verification behaviors.
